We have applied 29646 to target, got product(s). The apply_template returned three possible precursors (tuples). The result is a tuple of tuples? It gave three possible outcomes: each is a tuple of SMILES strings? Actually result: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO',))"

So three possible precursors each a single SMILES? Actually each inner tuple contains one SMILES. So we have three possible precursors after first step.

We need to continue with template 1914389 applied to each? The order must be exactly that sequence. So after first step, we apply 1914389 to the product(s) from step1. We applied to the first product (the one with Si group). It matched and gave two products: a tuple of two SMILES: ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC').

So that yields two fragments: one is a molecule still containing Si, the other is a fragment (maybe a reagent). For retrosynthesis, we need to break target into precursors; each step yields multiple precursors.

We need to continue applying next template 1914390 to the appropriate precursor(s). Likely to the Si-containing fragment? Let's check matching for each.

We tried matching 1914390 to the Si-containing product after step2: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and got False. Maybe need to apply to other product from step1? Let's try applying 1914390 to the second product from step1: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". Check matching.
